2027-03-16.title: Tuesday of the Fifth Week of Lent
readings: Whenever a serpent bit someone, that person would look at the serpent of bronze and live
O Lord, listen to my prayer and let my cry for help reach you
When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he
2027-03-16.alt: Lenten weekday of the fifth week. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. From the Fifth Sunday of Lent crosses and images may be veiled until the Passion is celebrated (where the bishops' conference allows). Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-03-16.verse: So Jesus said, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he, and that I do nothing on my own, but I speak these things as the Father instructed me.”
theo: The people of Israel are on the long road around Edom, and they lose patience. They complain against God and against Moses: why did you bring us out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? “There is no food and no water, and we detest this miserable food.” The miserable food is the manna, the bread from heaven. Then poisonous serpents come among them, and many die. The people confess, “We have sinned,” and Moses prays for them. God's remedy is strange: “Make a poisonous serpent, and set it on a pole; and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live.” Moses makes a serpent of bronze, and whoever looks at it lives. The very image of what was killing them, lifted up, becomes the sign of healing. The book of Wisdom later explains that it was not the bronze that saved them but God, the Saviour of all (Wisdom 16:7), and King Hezekiah would one day break the bronze serpent because people had begun to burn incense to it (2 Kings 18:4). The sign points beyond itself. The Psalm is the cry of all who are dying in the desert: “Hear my prayer, O LORD; let my cry come to you,” and its confidence that the Lord looks down from heaven “to set free those who were doomed to die.”

Jesus himself gave us the key to this reading when he said to Nicodemus: “just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life” (John 3:14–15). In today's Gospel he speaks of the same lifting up: “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he.” In John's Gospel, to be lifted up means two things at once: to be raised on the cross and to be exalted in glory. “I am he” echoes the name God revealed to Moses at the burning bush, “I AM.” On the cross, where Jesus looks most powerless, his divine identity will be revealed. He who bears the poison of our sin is lifted up, and whoever looks to him in faith lives. Jesus also warns that those who refuse to believe “will die in your sins”; the remedy is offered, but it must be looked at. These days the crucifix in our churches may be veiled in purple. The veil teaches us to long for the moment on Good Friday when it will be uncovered and we will be invited: behold the wood of the Cross. Then we will look, and live.
outline: Ask: where do you look when you are hurting?
Complaining about the bread from heaven.
The Son of Man lifted up on the cross.
“When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he.”
live: Spend five quiet minutes today simply looking at a crucifix, and tell Jesus what is poisoning your life.
For one whole day, turn every complaint into a short prayer of trust.
2027-03-16.prayer: Lord Jesus, lifted up on the cross like the serpent in the desert, we look to you and live. Heal the poison of our sin, forgive our complaining, and teach us to trust the Father on the long road. Show us that you are he, the Son who always does what pleases the Father. Amen.
altar: At Mass the priest lifts up the Host and the chalice: behold the Lamb of God. We look at the one who was lifted up on the cross, and we receive the medicine of eternal life.

quick: Israel grew impatient and complained against God and the manna.
God told Moses to lift up a bronze serpent; whoever looked at it lived.
Jesus, lifted up on the cross, reveals that he is I AM and gives life to all who look to him.
2027-03-16.action: Pray today before a crucifix, at home or in church, for five minutes.
2027-03-16.question: What is the poison in my life that I need to bring to the cross of Jesus?

family.explain: On the long walk through the desert God's people grumbled and said they hated the bread God gave them. Snakes bit them and they became sick. God told Moses to put a snake made of bronze on a pole. Whoever looked at it got better! Jesus said: I will be lifted up on the cross like that, so that everyone who looks to me will live.
family.intention: We pray for all who are sick, and for those who have lost hope.
family.ask: Ask: “What do we grumble about at home? Can we say thank you to God for it instead?”

illus: A nurse in a Kozhikode hospital kept a small crucifix in her pocket during night duty. A young man brought in after a snakebite was terrified while they waited for the anti-venom to work. She did not preach. She put the crucifix in his hand and said: hold this and breathe. Months later he came back to thank her and said: I did not know the story of Moses then. I only knew that someone had been hurt more than me and was holding on.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, lifted up on the cross, we look to you. Heal us and give us life. Amen.
share: The people became impatient on the way (Numbers 21:4). Where am I impatient with God?
Everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live (Numbers 21:8). What wound do I need to bring to Jesus?
When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he (John 8:28). What does the cross tell me about who Jesus is?
pm.resp: O Lord, listen to my prayer and let my cry for help reach you.
interc: For all who are seriously ill, especially victims of snakebite and accidents, and for those who care for them.
For those tired of the journey of faith, that they may not give up.
For those who complain and are bitter, that they may learn gratitude.
For all who will be baptized at Easter, that they may look to Christ and live.
For our group, that we may stay close to the cross this Holy Week.
pm.close: Father, you lifted up your Son on the cross to be our healing. Draw all people to him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the people of Israel were tired of walking and tired of the manna. They said: we detest this miserable food (Numbers 21:5). The bread from heaven had become boring. Poisonous serpents came, and many died. Then they confessed: we have sinned.

God gave Moses a strange remedy: make a serpent of bronze and set it on a pole; whoever is bitten shall look at it and live (Numbers 21:8). The very image of what was killing them became the sign of healing, because God chose to heal through it.

Jesus told Nicodemus: just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up (John 3:14). And today he says: when you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he (John 8:28). On the cross Jesus takes the poison of our sin into himself. And there, where he seems weakest, he is revealed as I AM, the Son of God.

Our crosses may be veiled in purple this week. On Good Friday they will be uncovered and we will be invited to look and adore. Let us begin now: look at the crucifix, bring him our wounds, stop complaining and trust. Whoever looks to him in faith will live. Amen.
kids: Children, when God's people were bitten by snakes, God told Moses to lift up a bronze snake on a pole. Whoever looked at it got better! Jesus was lifted up on the cross so that everyone who looks at him with love can be healed from sin. Look at a cross today and say: thank you, Jesus!

intro: Theme: “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he.”
From the serpent on the pole to the Son on the cross: look and live.

q: The people spoke against God and against Moses, “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? For there is no food and no water, and we detest this miserable food.”
And do not complain as some of them did, and were destroyed by the destroyer.
points.apply: Turn every complaint today into a prayer of thanks or of trust.

sub: Healing through the image of the wound.
q: And the LORD said to Moses, “Make a poisonous serpent, and set it on a pole; and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live.”
And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.
points.apply: Pray for five minutes before a crucifix each day of Holy Week.

q: God said to Moses, “I am who I am.”
So Jesus said, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will realize that I am he, and that I do nothing on my own, but I speak these things as the Father instructed me.”
points.apply: On Good Friday, come to venerate the Cross, and tell Jesus in your own words that you believe he is the Son of God.

concl: God heals through what is lifted up before our eyes.
On the cross Jesus is revealed as the Son, and whoever looks to him in faith lives.
2027-03-16.resolve: Look at the crucifix each day this week and pray: Jesus, you are he; heal me.
